g-glossary-s-w.title: Glossary definitions S-W (Start-to-Start to Work Performance Reports)
g-glossary-s-w.notes: SS; statement of work (narrative description of products, services or results to be delivered); statistical sampling; successor activity; summary activity; SWOT analysis; tacit knowledge (personal, hard to articulate - beliefs, experience, insights); tailoring (determining the appropriate combination of processes, inputs, tools, techniques, outputs and life cycle phases); team charter (team values, agreements, operating guidelines and expectations of acceptable behaviour); team management plan (component of the resource management plan describing when and how members are acquired and how long they are needed - glossary-only term); technique vs tool (technique = defined systematic procedure employed by a human resource, possibly using tools; tool = something tangible such as a template or software program); templates (partially complete documents in a predefined format); test and evaluation documents; threat (risk with a negative effect); three-point estimating (average or weighted average of optimistic, pessimistic and most likely estimates); threshold (predetermined value of a measurable variable that requires action if reached); T&M contract; TCPI; tolerance (quantified acceptable variation for a quality requirement); tornado diagram (special bar chart in sensitivity analysis comparing variables' relative importance); total float; trend analysis (mathematical models forecasting outcomes from historical results); trigger condition (event or situation indicating a risk is about to occur); unanimity; update (modification to any deliverable, plan component or document not under formal change control) vs change (modification to a formally controlled item); validation (assurance the product meets the needs of the customer and stakeholders) vs verification (evaluation of compliance with a regulation, requirement, specification or imposed condition) - the Validate Scope / Control Quality distinction; variance and variation (actual condition differing from the expected baseline condition); variance analysis; VAC; verified deliverables; virtual teams; voice of the customer (translating customer requirements into technical requirements for each phase of product development); WBS, WBS component (any level), WBS dictionary, work package (lowest level, cost and duration estimated and managed); work performance data, information (data from controlling processes analysed against plan components, documents and other WPI) and reports.
